newsitem.title: USA: Marathon has targeted 50 pct profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Marathon has targeted 50 pct profit rise.

text.p: USX Marathon Group has targeted a 50 percent increase in net income over the next three years, Victor G. Beghini, president of Marathon Oil Co said Thursday.

Excluding special items, one-time charges and credits, Marathon posted estimated adjusted net income of $529 million in 1996 -- more than four times 1993's adjusted net income, he told the PaineWebber energy conference.
Adjusted operating income was just over $1 billion last year, he noted.
"We were led by a continued strong performance in exploration and production," Beghini said. "In fact, upstream operating income has nearly doubled in each of the last three years."
Besides the income performance, Marathon fulfilled a "very ambitious" debt reduction goal -- exceeding a three-year, $1 billion debt reduction objective by $229 million, he noted.
He said other Marathon financial goals include:
-- Achieving a 12 percent return on capital employed by 1998. Marathon registered a 10.4 percent return in 1996 -- a 41-percent improvement over 1995.
-- Attaining a cash-flow interest coverage multiple of eight in 1999. Marathon raised that to 5.4 in 1996.
Beghini said Marathon's capital, investment and exploration budget for 1997 is $1.215 billion -- up 43 percent from 1996 actual spending of $851 million.
Comparable levels to the 1997 budget are projected for 1998 and 1999 to fund further growth, he said.
Marathon Oil is the main operating unit of USX-Marathon, a USX Corp subsidiary. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
